n_start: Rell's Gate is the last town before the Deep Road goes under the mountains, and in midwinter it is mostly a lit doorway in a wall of rock. The company is known here, which is new: the gate watch counts you in by name, and somebody has already told them what is wrapped in salt-cloth in the captain's pack. Orr's summons was waiting at the third station and has been read aloud twice since.
a0_tower: Captain Sabinne Orr, Warden of the Deep Road, does not offer anybody a chair. Sixteen Mile Tower has sent no lamp report for five weeks, the couriers are still running past it on schedule, and she wants the tower's road-book brought up the road and put on her desk. She has fourteen Wardens for two hundred miles of tunnel, and she says that number twice.
a0_tower_q: Her account is short and she does not decorate it. One patrol turned back at the Marchgate without a written reason; the second came home a man short, and the man they lost would not stop counting in a language nobody could place. The Marchgate itself was found unbarred, and the bar was on the inside where somebody had set it down neatly.
a0_haggle: Orr has no coin available anywhere in her district and says so before you can ask her for any. What she has instead is the Deep Road oath, sworn on the road-stone in front of the watch, which makes the company Warden-sworn on her road and answerable on it in both directions. It is worth considerably more than money underground, and it cannot be given back afterwards.
a0_charter: The oath is sworn on the road-stone with the entire gate watch standing out in the cold to witness it, and a clerk enters the Ninth Sword into the Deep Road roll. Dellach's expression throughout belongs to a man who was a Warden sergeant once and never expected to be counted as one again. Nyre records the exact wording twice, in two different books.
a0_sign: The commission is sealed at the bottom with wax that will not set properly in the cold. Then Orr gives her condition quietly, as though it were housekeeping: the road-book comes out above everything else, because the lamp hours written in it are the only reason anybody walks that road alive. She has buried four people who walked it on the wrong hour.
a0_guide: Ossa Vend is nineteen and has walked the Lamp Road twice a week since she was twelve, carrying her father's lighting pole and, since autumn, her father's debts. She wants a half share and the debts cleared, in that order, and she can recite the eleven lamp stations forwards and backwards. She does not ask what happened at Sixteen Mile, which is interesting.
a0_guide_hired: Ossa is hired and her mother's debts are cleared in front of a Reckoning clerk, which takes longer than the hiring. She carries her own lamp-pole and will not let anybody else carry it, and she is on the paving inspecting the first bracket before the rest of the company has finished loading. Vurma approves of her immediately and says nothing.
a0_dispatch: The tower's last report is five weeks old and reads as routine until the final page, where the hand deteriorates badly. Folded inside it are the route charts: eleven lamp stations, the hour each is lit and trimmed, and the standing intervals between them. Against the ninth station the tower captain has pencilled four words: the hours have changed.
a0_taproom: The Lamp and Ladder is half dwarf and half Warden and entirely underground, warm from a flue that runs somewhere useful. A road-mason is drinking steadily through what he saw at the ninth station, telling it to anybody who sits down. The Sable Guild has the table by the flue and is watching the company arrive with the specific attention of people who have opinions about surface companies.
a0_rumors: A round bought for the room produces the road's own version of the news. The couriers are running the lower march in daylight now, which has never happened. Two Reckoning priests went down in autumn and neither came up, and a coach with southern horses came through in the same week with its curtains drawn and its clerk paying the toll in silver.
a0_lamps: Sober enough to be exact, the road-mason is exact about the ninth station. The lamps there are lit an hour before the charts allow, and the count that goes with the lighting runs backwards, which no lamp-lighter on the road has ever done. He walked out over the shoulder in snow rather than pass it, and he has not been paid since.
a0_lamps_full: The rest of it costs him nothing to say and he says it flatly. His mate went on down the Lamp Road to argue about the hours, because the hours are a mason's business as much as anybody's. His kit came back up eight days later on a courier's barrow, with the tools still wrapped in their canvas and the canvas still tied.
a0_brawl: A Sable Guild delver has an opinion about surface companies walking dwarf roads, and he is delivering it in two languages so that nobody in the room misses any of it. Dellach sets his cup down flat, which is how it always begins with him. The Guild foreman watches without intervening, apparently interested in the outcome for professional reasons.
a0_brawl_win: It takes two exchanges and a broken bench. The delver sits down harder than he intended and stays sitting, and the Guild foreman calls it fair in front of the whole room, which is worth more than the fight. Nyre binds Dellach's hand afterwards and mentions, without emphasis, that he is forty-four years old.
a0_brawl_bought: A round is bought for the Guild table and the delver's grievance is heard out in full, which takes some time and involves three separate historical examples. At the end of it he gives you directions to the old drift entrance. He also gives you the name of the survey crew that walled it, thrown in as a courtesy nobody asked for.
a0_rest: A night in a dwarf bunkroom cut into the gatehouse rock, warm from the flue, with the door barred and no watch to keep. The company sleeps properly for the first time since Gallowmere, and it shows in the morning in the way everybody picks up their kit. Ossa sleeps sitting upright against her lamp-pole and denies it afterwards.
a0_yard: The caravan yard lies under a foot of snow, with one Sable Guild train loading for the lower march and a Rooks banner pitched over the only covered bay in it. A dwarf sits on her own kit at the yard's edge with no company at all. She is watching the Guild train load, and correcting their lashings under her breath, and not offering to help.
a0_ilsabet: Vurma Kell, pathfinder, was put out of the Sable Guild for filing a report about the ninth station that her own foreman burned in front of her. She made a copy before she filed it, which is either professional caution or spite, and she is candid that she does not know which. She wants a share and a witness.
a0_ilsabet_full: A full share agreed, and the burned report's copy handed over unasked before the coin is even counted out. Inside ten minutes she and Ilsabet are arguing about dwarf orthography over the same page, and both of them are visibly enjoying it. Kettle carries the dwarf's kit across the yard without being asked, which is a formal endorsement.
a0_ilsabet_half: A half share, taken flatly, with the copy of the report staying in her own coat where she can reach it. She will do exactly what she is paid to do and not one yard further, and she says so in advance so that nobody can claim afterwards to have been surprised by it.
a0_spears: The road-porters are Halt and Weem, cheap and willing and entirely unbothered by the details of the commission. They have carried for Guild trains as far as the fourth station and never once past it. They mention the fourth station three times during the negotiation without appearing to notice that they are doing it.
w0_rooks: Vasse Corrow has a Warden charter of her own now, bought with what she learned about Kar Duhn from a company that told her nothing and a frontier that told her everything. She offers to take the Sixteen Mile contract off your hands as a professional courtesy. Her tone suggests she expects refusal and would like the refusal noted.
w0_rooks_drink: Corrow's own autumn, told over two cups and without much decoration. Eleven people went down the Lamp Road under her charter and nine came back up it. Her scout came out of the old drift counting in dwarf, which she does not speak, and died of it eleven days later in a Reckoning bed with the count still going.
w0_ledger: The Reckoning chapter house is cut into the gatehouse rock and kept warmer than the Warden tower, and Prior Enna Vask presides over it with the manner of somebody who has never once been late. On the duty board, in the current hand, is a name Nyre has not spoken aloud since Gallowmere. Ferrin Ostwyn, her brother, posted down the road in autumn.
w0_account: Nyre reads the chapter's road account aloud in the flat voice she keeps for bad news, and it takes eleven minutes. Nine deliveries were requisitioned down the Deep Road in nine months, and every requisition carries her brother's signature. Beside each entry, in the same hand, somebody has copied out the lamp hours for the station it went to.
w0_kit: Credit against the commission, spent properly on things that work underground: pitch, oil, dwarf candles, crampons, a second reservoir lamp and a coil of wire rope. Vurma insists on the wire rope, refuses to explain why, and then checks the coil twice more before it is loaded. The debt settles in behind the company like a second contract.
w0_indent: Vask's better offer is made kindly and without any pressure at all. Leave the tower alone, bring the Reckoning her own priest's papers instead of the road-book, and the chapter will carry the company's names and debts for nine years, term for term. She says the word nine twice while explaining the terms, and Nyre hears it both times.
w0_kettle: Kettle is in the gatehouse arch with her pack still roped shut, refusing to unpack it and refusing to explain. She has been under one mountain already this year, and the Deep Road is nine hundred miles of mountain with lamps in it. She has been sitting in that arch since the company arrived, listening to the floor.
w0_kettle_press: What she says, when she finally says it, is worse than the refusal. The count the couriers are using on this road is the same count she learned at eleven, in the same cadence, with the same pause before the ninth. She has been hearing it through the gatehouse floor at intervals ever since you walked in.
w0_rhyme: She sets the cadence out on the table with three cups and a knife, the way the crews did it underground, so that everybody in the company can recognise it in the dark from any direction. It takes four minutes. Nobody says anything at all when she finishes, and Ossa asks her to do it once more.
w0_betray: Orr is informed that the company's scout is unfit for the road, and Orr, who is short of people, offers a substitute from her own watch within the hour. A note goes into a Warden roll about a captain who reports honestly. Kettle is on the paving at the bell regardless and does not look at you for two days.
a0_gather: The last hour in Rell's Gate goes on kit checked twice and the gate lamps lit for the ninth hour by a lighter who does not hurry over any of it. At the end of the yard the mouth of the Deep Road stands open in the rock. It does not look like a tunnel from here; it looks like something holding its breath politely.
a0_march_light: Out at the bell with the Guild train's dust still hanging in the first mile, the road-lamps burning at their proper hours, and eight miles of good dwarf paving underfoot. For the first hour it is the easiest walking the company has had in a year, and everybody says so, and then everybody stops saying it.
a0_march_night: A night start to steal a march on the Guild train means six miles of unlit paving with two lamps between five people, and it works only in the narrow sense that you arrive at the junction first. The company gets there cold, half-blind and already spent on nothing. The day has not begun, and the charts put the next station four hours further on.
a0_supply: The advance sits on a Warden table with one morning available in which to spend it properly. Nyre wants a hand-barrow, salt and lamp oil, because the road is long and the stations are cold and empty. Vurma wants a second wire line and a moor-iron pick, because the drift is worse than the Guild admits in writing.
a0_supply_mule: A hand-barrow, four stone of salt, two casks of oil and a spare reservoir, which together make the most valuable load on the road and by some distance the slowest. Halt and Weem take the handles in shifts and complain in alternation. Nobody suggests leaving any of it behind, then or later.
a0_supply_blade: A moor-iron pick and forty feet of wire line, cold in the hand and heavier than it looks, bought off a smith who wrapped it without comment. If the old drift is as bad as the Sable Guild says in its own burned reports, both items will earn their weight twice over.
a0_muster: The first junction of the Deep Road lies eight miles under the mountain's shoulder, where the dwarves put a bench and a lamp and a survey pillar. The Lamp Road goes on straight and lit. The surface stair goes up over the shoulder into snow, and the old drift goes down and west into unlit dwarf work that nobody has serviced in a century.
e_a0_insult: You ride south from Rell's Gate with the oath unsworn and the tower unreported, and the weather closes behind you within a day. Corrow's chartered company goes down the Lamp Road inside a week on terms Orr would never have offered a stranger. What they find is somebody else's story, and nobody ever tells you how it ended.
e_a0_moor_night: Up the shoulder at night behind a drunk mason, to look down at the ninth station from above and settle the question. The lamps below are lit an hour early, exactly as he described, and the count that goes with them is running backwards. It is still running when it reaches the two of you, and it does not have to climb the slope to do it.
e_a0_gaol: Steel drawn in a Warden gatehouse puts the whole company in the gate cells before midnight, which is a fast piece of work by anybody's standard. The commission is struck at dawn and passed to the Rooks. Orr reads the forfeiture through the bars in a level voice and does not raise it once, which somehow makes it worse.
e_a0_sell: The Sixteen Mile contract is sold to Corrow in a covered bay for eighty crowns and a handshake with a witness. The company winters warm at Rell's Gate on the proceeds and is finished as a company by the thaw, because a road town is small and everybody in it knows who sold what and to whom.
e_a0_indenture: Vask's ink dries on nine years of the company's names before anybody has read the clause about her brother properly. The tower is left alone as agreed and the deliveries continue on schedule through the winter. Nyre walks out of her own chapter house without a word, because she has read the clause and will not explain it to you.
e_a0_walk: The commission is handed back across a Warden table with an honest reason attached, and Orr accepts it without argument because she has been refused before by better-funded companies. You winter at Rell's Gate. Every ninth night, at the ninth hour, something passes under the gatehouse floor counting, and nobody in the taproom looks up.
